source_text: Τοῦτον ἂν πείσειας, αὐτοκράτωρ, μεταφρονοῦντα, τοῖς ἀποστολικοῖς μὴ ἀντιτείνειν διδάγμασιν· ἢ τοῖς ἐν οἷς ἑάλω κακοδοξίας ἐγκείμενον ἀσεβήμασιν, ἄρδην τῆς Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἀφανίσειας ἐπαύλεως, ὡς ἂν μὴ τῆς θολερᾶς αὐτοῦ λογοθωπείας τὰς τῶν ἁπλουστέρων ψυχὰς ἐργάσηται θέραμα.
orientation: Eustathius, having accused Arius of denying the Son's consubstantiality and numbering the Creator with creation, now addresses the emperor directly with a two-part request.
pass_a_gloss: If you should persuade this man, emperor, to change his mind, that he not oppose the apostolic teachings; or if he remains fixed in the impious acts of false teaching in which he has been caught, may you remove him utterly from the fold of Christ and of us, so that his muddy sophistry may not make the souls of the simpler ones its prey.

choices.why: The participle describes the desired state of Arius if persuaded; 'change his mind' captures the shift from his current false teaching.
The verb means to set oneself against; 'oppose' keeps the active resistance to apostolic teaching.
The participle with the dative indicates persisting in a state; 'remains fixed in' conveys obstinate adherence.
The optative expresses a wish; 'remove utterly' captures the force of destruction or disappearance from the fold.
The term denotes a dwelling or sheepfold; 'fold' preserves the pastoral image of the Church as Christ's and the faithful's enclosure.
The noun means something hunted or caught; 'prey' fits the metaphor of sophistry ensnaring souls.

pass_b_english: You could persuade him, Emperor, to change his mind and stop opposing the apostolic teachings. Or, if he remains fixed in the impious acts of false teaching in which he has been caught, may you remove him utterly from the Church, the fold of Christ and of us, so that his muddy sophistry may not make prey of simpler souls.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἄρδην τῆς Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἀφανίσειας ἐπαύλεως
last_rejected.why: Optative ἀφανίσειας is wish/prayer, not possibility; 'may you' softens to wish but loses the direct petition force.
last_rejected.fix: would that you might remove him utterly
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπαύλεως with optative ἀφανίσειας expresses wish/petition; 'may you remove' captures this adequately.

last_rejected.quote: from the fold of Christ and of us
last_rejected.why: ἐπαύλεως means 'farmstead/estate' metaphorically 'fold'; but 'Christ and of us' should be 'of Christ and us'—the Greek shows joint possession, English slightly awkward.
last_rejected.fix: from the fold of Christ and us
last_rejected.ruling: 'of Christ and of us' renders τῆς Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν acceptably; slight awkwardness, not a meaning change.

problems.why: Unusual collocation; 'muddy' likely means 'turbid, confused' but sounds odd to modern ear.

problems.quote: the impious acts of false teaching
problems.why: Arius's error is doctrinal, not active 'acts'; awkward rendering of Greek plural for teachings.
'Church' and 'fold of Christ' refer to the same body; reader may think two groups are meant.
problems.fix: Use 'Church' in both places or add 'the Church, the fold of Christ'.

edits.old: the impious acts of false teaching
the fold of Christ and of us
edits.new: the Church, the fold of Christ and of us

fixed: Changed 'the impious acts of false teaching' to 'the impious false teachings' to reflect doctrinal error rather than active deeds.
Added 'the Church' before 'the fold of Christ and of us' to clarify that both refer to the same body.

problems.why: Awkward compound; 'muddying' as active participle is unidiomatic.
Singular vs. plural for same concept; minor but could suggest different categories of error.
problems.fix: Standardize to singular or plural throughout.

fixed: Changed 'muddying sophistry' to 'muddy sophistry' to avoid the unidiomatic active participle.
Changed 'impious false teachings' to 'impious acts of false teaching' to match the singular 'false teaching' in the source and glossary.
